evidence.text: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take the whole army with you, and go up and attack Ai. See, I have delivered into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
you are to rise from the ambush and seize the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.
And when you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has commanded! See, I have given you orders.”
Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Hold out your battle lance toward Ai, for into your hand I will deliver the city.” So Joshua held out his battle lance toward Ai,
Israel took for themselves only the cattle and plunder of that city, as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
At that time Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel,

just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: “an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used.” And on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings.

All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel.

And there in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written.

All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua failed to read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them.

c: Joshua

Joshua, son of Nun, was Moses’ assistant and successor as Israel’s leader. Joshua brought the young nation across the Jordan River into the Promised Land of Canaan, faithfully following God’s leadership.
Before Israel reached Mount Sinai, Joshua led Israel’s warriors when Amalek attacked Israel (
). Shortly thereafter, he was among the twelve men Moses sent to scout the Promised Land (
). Against popular opinion, Joshua and Caleb urged Israel to occupy Canaan immediately (
), and as a result, of the twelve spies, only they entered Canaan (
God directed Moses to designate Joshua as his successor (
). After Moses died, Joshua led Israel across the Jordan River (
) to the conquest of Jericho (
). When Israel suffered defeat at Ai, Joshua turned to the Lord and followed his instructions to purge Israel of sin (
); then Israel conquered Ai (
). Following God’s instructions to Moses (
), Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal (
) and read the blessings and curses of the covenant (
). Joshua conducted campaigns against two coalitions of Canaanite kings, a southern and a northern coalition (
). Joshua’s victories in these campaigns opened the hill country to settlement by the Israelites.
After supervising the allotment of territories to the tribes of Israel, Joshua received his own portion in the land of Ephraim (
). He established the cities of refuge (
) and the Levitical cities (ch
) and released the 2½ tribes that had settled east of the Jordan River to return home (
). As he grew old, Joshua charged Israel to remain faithful to God (

). His farewell message at Shechem summarized God’s dealings with Israel and concluded with the familiar challenge, “Choose today whom you will serve. . . . But as for me and my family, we will serve the
Lord
). Joshua died at the age of 110 and was buried in Timnath-serah (
Joshua demonstrated exceptional faithfulness throughout his life, except in dealing with the Gibeonites (
), when he neglected to consult the Lord regarding a decision. Israel served God faithfully under Joshua and the elders Joshua trained (
). Stephen mentions Joshua in his martyr’s sermon (
), and the writer of Hebrews uses Joshua’s conquest of Jericho as an illustration of faith (
). It is fitting that Joshua and Jesus are the same name in Hebrew: Joshua led Israel into physical salvation in Canaan; Jesus leads all who believe in him into eternal salvation.

Shechem

Shechem was strategically located at the entrance to the pass between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, where it could control several key roads through the central hill country. Jacob bought land near Shechem (
). While there, Jacob’s daughter, Dinah, was raped by the prince of the area (whose name was Shechem); in response, two of Dinah’s brothers, Simeon and Levi, killed all the men of the land (
). Later, the town of Shechem became part of Joseph’s inheritance (
) and one of the cities of refuge (see
During the period of the judges, Gideon’s son Abimelech ruled from Shechem (
). Solomon later fortified Shechem as a provincial capital, but it was sacked soon after, probably by Shishak of Egypt when he invaded Israel in 926
BC
(see
). Jeroboam I then refortified the city and made it the capital of the kingdom of Israel (
). Shechem was again destroyed, this time by the Assyrian king Shalmaneser V, in 724
BC
, shortly before the destruction of Samaria, and the ruins were virtually uninhabited for about four hundred years.

The first attempt to conquer Ai had been done without consulting God; the second attempt would be made at God’s command and direction. Before the second attempt, God spoke to Joshua again and gave him a strategy. More importantly, in light of Israel’s recent disaster, God gave him encouragement and a promise.

This ceremony marked the formal possession of the land, even though major campaigns against the Canaanites were still to come. The ritual of sacrifice and reading of the law highlighted the promises and obligations of God’s covenant with them and anticipated the eventual possession of all of Canaan.
